source.title: Whitening and Second Order Optimization Both Make Information in the Dataset Unusable During Training, and Can Reduce or Prevent Generalization
source.authors: Neha S. Wadia; Daniel Duckworth; S. Schoenholz; Ethan Dyer; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that whitening and unregularized second-order optimization can reduce or prevent generalization, and that regularization can change the outcome. It does not test random-label memorization or any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper tests whitening and second-order optimization on natural-label classification tasks. It does not test fitting random labels, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks as the intervention, adaptive first-order optimizers, minibatch size, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Reported figure-only values are recorded as figure only; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests whitening and exact second-order optimization, neither of which is an intervention named by V1–V8. Its Gauss-Newton comparisons do not test V4's adaptive first-order optimizers. It neither tests nor operationally uses a listed claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove information restrictions under specified architectural and initialization assumptions, empirically find that whitening and unregularized second-order optimization can harm generalization while accelerating convergence, and show that regularized Gauss-Newton can sometimes improve test performance.
record.recipe_differences: Tests whitening and second-order optimization on natural-label datasets rather than random-label memorization, width, batch size, dropout, or the listed sharpness and memorized-example measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Whitening severity depends on whether whitening uses training data or the full dataset and on dataset size relative to input dimension/rank. Regularized Gauss-Newton results vary with regularizer strength; intermediate values can improve test loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Full whitening produces chance-level generalization in the high-dimensional linear and MLP settings; train-only whitening also worsens performance. Whitening penalties persist in larger datasets and in a convolutional network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whitening can remove information useful for generalization, with effects depending on whitening procedure, dataset size, input rank, and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Unregularized Gauss-Newton yields higher test loss despite lower training loss; intermediate preconditioner regularization can yield lower test loss than gradient descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact second-order optimization can impair generalization, while suitable preconditioner regularization can preserve faster convergence and sometimes improve held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 139, 2021
record.problems: The WRN result uses two seeds. Several conclusions are reported qualitatively from figures without exact values in the text. The MLP experiments use different whitening procedures and test-set constructions, including full-whitened test examples included in the transform. The study does not test random-label memorization or the claim versions listed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated numeric outcomes were available in the text beyond the recorded findings; detailed figure values were not transcribed because they are figure-only and not stated numerically in prose.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive first-order optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on data size, strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row maps to none; this does not dispute the reported whitening or Gauss-Newton effects. No additional result bearing on a listed version appears in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
No network-width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison of adaptive first-order optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
No minibatch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: linear model
rows.size_stated: 512-dimensional inputs; linear map to 10-dimensional one-hot labels
rows.operation_detail: Full data whitening followed by gradient descent; test error measured at the lowest validation error.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10 features from an untrained four-layer convolutional network

rows.baseline: Unwhitened gradient descent generalizes better; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative result; no numeric error is given there.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. The linear readout in Fig. 4(a) is initialized to zero, not randomly; the feature-producing CNN is randomly initialized. The reported test metric is squared loss on one-hot labels, so the qualitative chance-level statement should not be presented as a measured classification error rate.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.stage_stated: trained from Xavier initialization with full-batch gradient descent until training error was below 10^-3
rows.operation_detail: ZCA train-whitening followed by full-batch gradient descent; test accuracy measured at the highest validation accuracy.
rows.baseline: Unwhitened WRN; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Underperforms the unwhitened WRN; a gap persists beyond input dimensionality.
rows.uncertainty: Means and standard errors across two seeds are plotted; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper notes this result occurs despite the convolutional input layer and Xavier initialization violating theoretical requirements.
rows.check: The whitening comparison measures none of V1–V8. Its convolutional architecture does not make this a convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison.

rows.subject: CNN with ResNet-50 convolutional block and two dense layers
rows.stage_stated: trained to 100% training accuracy; best validation checkpoint evaluated
rows.operation_detail: Unregularized Gauss-Newton optimization on unwhitened data.
rows.baseline: Full-batch gradient descent on the same CNN; exact loss not stated.
rows.value: Higher test loss than gradient descent despite lower training loss.
rows.uncertainty: Averages over five seeds are plotted; error bars indicate twice the standard error in the mean.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the result, not exact values.
rows.check: Exact Gauss-Newton versus full-batch gradient descent does not measure V4's adaptive first-order optimizer comparison.

conditions.value: intermediate λ; exact values for lower test loss not stated in text

rows.baseline: Full-batch gradient descent; exact loss not stated.
rows.value: For some λ values, lower test loss than gradient descent.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate twice the standard error in the mean across five seeds.
rows.note: The text says the result occurs at intermediate regularization values; it interprets the benefit as potentially dataset- and model-inductive-bias-dependent.
rows.check: Regularizing an exact Gauss-Newton preconditioner does not test V4's tuning, weight-decay, or optimizer-switching conditions.
